location: NIST Handbook 135 (2020): equation 3-7 p29/PDF61; Figure 3-1 p26/PDF58; section 3.3.1 p34/PDF66; section 4.3.1 pp44-45/PDF76-77; section 6.1.1 p78/PDF110
text: Source-based paraphrase and mathematical transcription, checked 2026-10-29. Equation 3-7: PV = A0 * ((1 + d)^t - 1) / (d * (1 + d)^t). A0 is a uniform annual amount, d the annual discount rate, and t years. Its reference example uses $100 annually over five years at 3%, giving $457.97. Figure 3-1 also gives the sum of year-end discount factors from year 1 through n. Section 3.3.1 Method 1 specifies future costs AND savings in constant dollars discounted at a real rate excluding general inflation; price bases must not be mixed. Section 4.3.1 recommends discounting annual amounts from each service-year end. Section 6.1.1 discounts operating savings St and subtracts discounted incremental investments. Declared application assumptions, not source measurements: annual is baseline-minus-alternative operating savings, constant in real terms, without escalation, maintenance differences or replacements. Apply the equal-amount factor to this conditional savings stream. The profile's home, period bounds and positive-rate restriction are application scope; empirical savings, zero rates, variable cashflows and universal forecasting are not claimed.
